faq.q: Does FUSE give me an ISO 27001 certificate?
faq.a: No. It maps each stage to ISO 27001:2022 Annex A controls and produces reports that support an audit.
Keys are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM and are never sent to the browser.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, and Ollama for local models.
No. You can download the code as a ZIP. GitHub is optional, for pushes and pull requests.

faq.q: How is the security score calculated?
faq.a: From deterministic Semgrep and Trivy scans. A score that only comes from the AI is labelled differently.

landing.closingLede: Five gates, one guided workspace, and evidence you can show.
landing.problemStat: AI-generated code introduced risky security flaws in 45% of tests.
landing.problemStatSource: Veracode, 2025 GenAI Code Security Report (October 2025 update)
problemList: Code arrives in minutes but is seldom checked for injection, weak authentication or leaked secrets.
Mapping to a standard usually happens after the app is built, when every change is already expensive.
Without an artefact per stage it is hard to show which control was met, and when.
limits: Not an ISO 27001 or NIST certification; FUSE maps controls and prepares evidence
Scanners find known patterns; human review is still needed
AI output quality depends on the model you choose
Docker is required to run apps and scans

analysis.name: Analysis & Requirements
analysis.desc: Scope the website, recommend language/stack, define security requirements & data classification.

scope.label: Project Scope & Objectives

stack.label: Stack Recommendation
stack.detail: Select language, framework, database, and hosting with security justification.

security.label: Security & Privacy Requirements

data.label: Data Classification

recommendations.label: Security Recommendations (≥3)
recommendations.detail: Provide at least 3 actionable security recommendations with step-by-step guidance.

design.name: Design & Architecture
design.desc: UI/UX layout, threat model, architecture diagram, database schema and auth flow design.

ui.label: UI/UX Design & Page Layout
ui.detail: Design page layout, wireframes, color palette, and component structure.

architecture.label: Architecture & Data Flow
architecture.detail: Define component architecture, trust boundaries, and system interactions.

stride.label: STRIDE Threat Model
stride.detail: Identify threats, impact, likelihood, and mitigation strategies.

diagram.label: Mermaid Architecture Diagram
diagram.detail: Generate visual architecture and data flow diagrams.

schema.label: Database Schema & Auth Flow
schema.detail: Design database models, relationships, and authentication/authorization flow.

recommendations.label: Architecture Security Recommendations (≥3)
recommendations.detail: Provide at least 3 architecture security recommendations with actionable steps.

development.name: Secure Development
development.desc: Implement UI/frontend pages and generate secure source code with NIST PW.5 secure coding.

frontend.label: Frontend & UI Implementation
frontend.detail: Generate responsive page layouts, UI components, and styling based on design.

scaffold.label: Project Scaffolding & Config
scaffold.detail: Set up project structure, configuration, environment templates, and CI security.

auth.label: Authentication & Authorization
auth.detail: Implement secure user authentication, password hashing, and session management.

antiInjection.label: Anti-Injection & Output Encoding
antiInjection.detail: Implement parameterized queries/ORM and XSS output encoding.

secrets.label: Secrets Handling & CSRF Protection
secrets.detail: Implement CSRF protection, environment secrets management, and safe error handling.

recommendations.label: Secure Coding Recommendations (≥3)
recommendations.detail: Provide at least 3 secure coding recommendations with action steps.

testing.name: Security Testing & Audit
testing.desc: Scan for vulnerabilities, assess security score, and auto-fix issues.

owasp.label: OWASP Top 10 Review
owasp.detail: Audit generated source code files for OWASP Top 10 security vulnerabilities.

score.label: Security Score Assessment
score.detail: Calculate security score (0–100) based on vulnerability findings and compliance.

remediation.label: Remediation & Fix Suggestions
remediation.detail: Generate code fixes for identified security findings for user review.

recommendations.label: Security Audit Recommendations (≥3)
recommendations.detail: Provide at least 3 security audit recommendations with actionable steps.

handover.name: Handover & Deliverables
handover.desc: Export source code to ZIP or push to GitHub with full documentation and ISO report.

manual.label: Manual Book & Documentation
manual.detail: Generate deployment guide, environment setup, endpoints, and page documentation.

compliance.label: ISO 27001 Compliance Report
compliance.detail: Generate ISO 27001 Annex A crosswalk report and NIST SSDF compliance summary.

checklist.label: Release Security Checklist
checklist.detail: Verify secure defaults, backup configuration, audit logging, and deployment readiness.

export.label: Source Code Export & GitHub Push
export.detail: Prepare source code bundle (ZIP) or push to connected GitHub repository.

recommendations.label: Final Release Recommendations (≥3)
recommendations.detail: Provide at least 3 release security recommendations with actionable steps.

marketplace.name: Marketplace
marketplace.desc: Many sellers open stores on one site. Buyers browse products, leave reviews and pay in a single cart.

checks.orderAccess: Checks whether a user can open someone else's orders.
checks.paymentWebhook: Checks whether the payment webhook is validated before an order is marked paid.
checks.reviewXss: Checks whether review text can inject scripts (XSS).

ecommerce.name: Online store
ecommerce.desc: One store with a catalog, product pages and checkout. Suits a business selling its own products.

checks.clientPrice: Checks whether prices can be changed from the client.
checks.checkoutCsrf: Checks whether checkout is protected against CSRF.
checks.buyerData: Maps which buyer data is sensitive and who may see it.

lms.name: Online course
lms.desc: A course catalog, a classroom with video and quizzes. Teachers manage material, students follow from anywhere.

checks.paidContent: Checks whether paid material can be opened without access.
checks.quizIntegrity: Checks whether quiz scores can be changed from the client.
checks.fileUpload: Checks which file types and sizes may be uploaded.

saas.name: SaaS dashboard
saas.desc: A subscription app with an overview, team and billing. Each organisation sees only its own data.

checks.tenantIsolation: Checks whether one tenant's data can be read by another tenant.
checks.roleAccess: Checks whether each role can only use the features it is allowed.
checks.secretsInCode: Checks whether secret keys are written directly in the code.

clinic.name: Clinic booking
clinic.desc: Patients see doctor schedules and book appointments. The clinic keeps visit history in one place.

checks.healthData: Maps which health data is sensitive and how it is stored.
checks.recordAuth: Checks whether patient history opens only for those entitled to it.
checks.formRateLimit: Checks whether the appointment form is rate limited against floods.

company.name: Company profile
company.desc: A company profile, a list of services and a contact form. The default template for projects without a specific category.

checks.contactSpam: Checks whether the contact form can be used for spam.
checks.securityHeaders: Checks HTTP security headers before the site is handed over.
checks.outdatedDeps: Checks for outdated dependencies with known vulnerabilities.

news.name: News portal
news.desc: A news front page, article pages and an editor panel. The newsroom writes, edits and publishes from one place.

checks.contentXss: Checks whether article content can inject scripts (XSS).
checks.editorRole: Checks whether only editors can publish articles.
checks.imageUpload: Checks which image types and sizes may be uploaded.

api.name: REST API docs
api.desc: Endpoint reference, code examples and API key management. Other developers can start using the API quickly.

checks.tokenAuth: Checks how auth tokens are issued, sent and revoked.
checks.rateLimit: Maps per-key request limits to prevent abuse.
checks.inputValidation: Checks whether every endpoint input is validated on the server.
